meta.title: Who really said "I'd rather drink sewer water than see Taylor Swift at the Super Bowl"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Elon Musk never said he'd rather drink sewer water than see Taylor Swift at the Super Bowl. The line began on a 2024 satire site; fact-checkers rate it False.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I'd rather drink sewer water than see Taylor Swift at the Super Bowl'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Elon Musk. Fact-checkers trace this line to a January 2024 satire article that spread on Facebook as a real quote. PolitiFact rated it False.

answer.label: Not Elon Musk — a satire-site fabrication
answer.authorDates: Self-described satire and parody news site · January 2024
answer.sourceLine: No record shows Musk ever said it. Fact-checkers trace the line to a January 2024 satire article on Esspots. Another satire site, PanoPerspectives, also ran it, and from there it spread on Facebook as if it were real. PolitiFact rated it False ↗.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from

docMeta.dd: Breaking: Elon Musk Says ‘I’d Rather Drink Sewer Water Than See Taylor Swift At The Super Bowl’
Esspots, a self-described satire site, January 2024
False (PolitiFact, Check Your Fact, Lead Stories); “Errado” (Observador)

source.excerpt: Breaking: Elon Musk Says ‘I’d Rather Drink Sewer Water Than See Taylor Swift At The Super Bowl’
trail: Feb. 9, 2024 — Check Your Fact ↗ rates the claim False. It finds that the story comes from PanoPerspectives, which calls itself a destination for “a satirical and comedic take on current events.” It adds that if Musk had said it, “media outlets would have covered it, yet none have.”
Feb. 27, 2024 — Portugal’s Observador ↗ rates it “Errado” (wrong). It also traces the line to the satire site PanoPerspectives.

June 4, 2024 — PolitiFact ↗ rates a May 23, 2024 Facebook post False. It finds “no credible news or public statements from Musk” and lists the Esspots and PanoPerspectives satire articles as the source.
June 4, 2024 — Lead Stories ↗ traces the meme to a Feb. 8, 2024 post by a Facebook page that says it posts satire, and traces the text itself to an Esspots satire article from January 2024.
source.excerptNote: This is the satire headline as PolitiFact lists it in its sources. Quotle did not fetch the Esspots page itself. The fact-checkers give different January 2024 dates for it: PolitiFact says Jan. 30 and Lead Stories says Jan. 20. Check Your Fact transcribes the circulating wording as “I would rather drink sewer water than see Taylor Swift at the Super Bowl.”

sourceLink.text: PolitiFact: Elon Musk didn't choose sewer water over Taylor Swift (June 4, 2024)

source.rightsNote: The wording comes from 2024 satire web articles (Esspots, PanoPerspectives), not from anything Musk said or wrote. A 2024 work is nowhere near the public domain, but whether a one-line satirical headline is protected, and who would own it, is unclear. Quotle therefore asserts no rights status.

author.bio: Esspots is a website that calls itself a satire and parody news outlet, according to Lead Stories ↗. PolitiFact and Lead Stories both trace the “sewer water” line to an Esspots article from January 2024. Check Your Fact and Observador found the same story on a second self-described satire site, PanoPerspectives.

copyAttribution: “I’d rather drink sewer water than see Taylor Swift at the Super Bowl” — falsely attributed to Elon Musk. It began as a January 2024 satire article (Esspots) and was rated False by PolitiFact (June 4, 2024).

misattribution.heading: How a satire headline became a “Musk quote”
misattribution.intro: This line was never a misremembered remark. It was written as satire, and once it was stripped of its satire label it got shared as a real quote.

items.why: No interview, post or public statement contains it. PolitiFact found “no credible news or public statements from Musk to corroborate the claim” (PolitiFact ↗).
PolitiFact and Lead Stories trace the text to an Esspots article from January 2024. Esspots calls itself a satire and parody news outlet (Lead Stories ↗).
Check Your Fact found the story there and noted that “the story itself has two tags stating it is satire” (Check Your Fact ↗).

Lead Stories traces the viral image to a Feb. 8, 2024 post by a page whose intro says “We post SATIRE, nothing on this page is real.” The image kept circulating after that, including in a May 23, 2024 post (Lead Stories ↗).
A few months earlier, Check Your Fact debunked a similar line: “No, Elon Musk Did Not Say He’d Rather Break His Leg Than See Taylor Swift At NFL Game” ↗ (Oct. 30, 2023).

misattribution.truthLine: Elon Musk did not say it. The line is satire, first published in January 2024 on self-described satire sites, and it spread as a real quote. PolitiFact rated it False ↗.

context.heading: Why it spread
lead: The line appeared in the weeks before the February 2024 Super Bowl, when Taylor Swift’s attendance at Kansas City Chiefs games was a running news story. At the time, Check Your Fact noted “debate about whether or not she will appear at the Super Bowl.” A celebrity rivalry that sounds plausible, plus a crude punchline, is the usual recipe for satire that gets shared as fact.
The fake also had a long life. The same wording was still being shared as real in May 2024, and four fact-checkers in two countries ended up debunking it.
context.pull: “If Musk had said that, media outlets would have covered it, yet none have.” — Check Your Fact
